phrases.title: Essential phrases
items: kya aap meri madad kar sakte hain?
kyaa aap MEH-ree MUH-dud kur SUK-teh hain
क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?

phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: Three "you": tu (very close, children, or rude), tum (friends, equals, younger), aap (polite, strangers, elders). Use aap when unsure. The verb changes too: tu bolta hai, tum bolte ho, aap bolte hain.

phrases.title: Survival
items: how do you say... in Hindi?
koh HIN-dee mayn kyaa KEH-teh hain

phrases.title: Getting around
items: what time does the train leave?

phrases.title: Shopping
items: do you have a smaller size?
kya main card se de sakta hoon?
kyaa main kaard seh day SUK-taa hoon
क्या मैं कार्ड से दे सकता हूँ?

phrases.title: Hotel and travel
items: I would like to change money

phrases.title: In the classroom
items: kya main andar aa sakta hoon?
kyaa main UN-dur aa SUK-taa hoon
क्या मैं अंदर आ सकता हूँ?
may I go to the toilet?
kya main shauchaalay jaa sakta hoon?
kyaa main show-chaa-LUY jaa SUK-taa hoon
क्या मैं शौचालय जा सकता हूँ?
I do not know the answer
maaf kijiye, mujhe der ho gayi
MAAF KEE-jee-yeh MOO-jheh dayr hoh GUH-yee
माफ़ कीजिए, मुझे देर हो गई
is shabd ka matlab kya hai?
is shubd kaa MUT-lub kyaa hai
इस शब्द का मतलब क्या है?
kya main kalam le sakta hoon?
kyaa main KUH-lum lay SUK-taa hoon
क्या मैं कलम ले सकता हूँ?

phrases.title: Phone and internet
items: kya main aapka phone istemaal kar sakta hoon?
kyaa main AAP-kaa phohn is-tay-MAAL kur SUK-taa hoon
क्या मैं आपका फ़ोन इस्तेमाल कर सकता हूँ?
where can I charge my phone?
main phone kahaan charge kar sakta hoon?
main phohn ku-HAAN charj kur SUK-taa hoon
मैं फ़ोन कहाँ चार्ज कर सकता हूँ?

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Hindi has no he / she difference in the pronoun for "he, she, it": vah. The verb shows the gender. aap is the polite "you".

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Masculine ending -aa becomes -e (ladkaa → ladke). Feminine -ee or -i becomes -iyaan (ladki → ladkiyaan), other feminine nouns add -en (kitaab → kitaaben). Many masculine nouns do not change (ghar).

grammar.title: To have (mere paas)
text: Hindi says "near me there is": mere paas... hai. For family: mere... hain.

grammar.title: Regular verbs (present tense)
text: Take the stem (verb minus -naa) + -taa / -te / -tee + hona. Bolna (to speak), man speaking:
ex: main bank mein kaam karta hoon
main bunk mayn kaam KUR-taa hoon
मैं बैंक में काम करता हूँ

grammar.title: Jaana: to go
ex: vah kharidaari ke liye jaa rahi hai
woh khu-ree-DAA-ree keh LEE-yeh jaa RUH-hee hai
वह ख़रीदारी के लिए जा रही है

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Word order is subject, object, verb (the verb is last). Adjectives come before the noun.
rows: Main aaj yahaan kaam karta hoon.
main aaj yuh-HAAN kaam KUR-taa hoon
ex: we live in a big house
hum bade ghar mein rehte hain
hoom BUH-deh gur mayn REH-teh hain
हम बड़े घर में रहते हैं
vah aaj yahaan kaam karta hai
woh aaj yuh-HAAN kaam KUR-taa hai
वह आज यहाँ काम करता है

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put nahin before the verb "hona" (or before the verb): main nahin jaata. In the present, nahin usually goes before the main verb.

Put nahin before the verb (usually right before "hai" or the main verb): main nahin jaata. "There is not" = nahin hai. In the present tense the "hona" part may be dropped: main nahin jaata (I do not go).
ex: I do not have a car
vah ravivaar ko kaam karta hai
woh RUH-vee-vaar koh kaam KUR-taa hai
वह रविवार को काम करता है
he does not work on Sundays
vah ravivaar ko kaam nahin karta
woh RUH-vee-vaar koh kaam nuh-HEEN KUR-taa
वह रविवार को काम नहीं करता

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Put kya at the start for a yes / no question, or raise your voice.

grammar.title: Possessives
text: Possessives agree with the thing owned: mera (m), meri (f), mere (pl m).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: tu for children and very close friends. tum for friends. aap for strangers and elders. "-ji" after a name is respect (Sharma-ji). Hum is also used for "I" in very formal speech.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: verb stem + -aa / -ee / -e (agrees with the doer). Future: stem + -oongaa (m) / -oongee (f).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Close friends: stem (aa, baitho). Friendly: stem + -o (aao, baitho). Polite: stem + -iye (aaiye, baithiye). Negative: mat + the command (mat aao) or nahin kijiye in polite speech.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: sakna = can (main tair sakta hoon), chaahiye / padna = must (mujhe jaana hai, mujhe jaana padega), chaahna = want (main khaana chahta hoon). Cannot = nahin sakta.
ex: kya aap meri madad kar sakte hain?
kyaa aap MEH-ree MUH-dud kur SUK-teh hain
क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?
I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Hindi uses words after the noun (postpositions): mein = in, par = on / at, ke neeche = under, ke paas = near, ke baghal mein = next to.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
dukaan bank ke baghal mein hai
doo-KAAN bunk keh BUG-ul mayn hai
दुकान बैंक के बग़ल में है
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add se (than) after the second thing, and zyaada (more): mujhse bada (bigger than me). Most = sabse + adjective: sabse bada.

grammar.title: Everyday sentences
text: Extra practice with the most useful patterns.
ex: ve har din kaam karte hain
woh hur din kaam KUR-teh hain
वे हर दिन काम करते हैं
